title: HR Navigates AI and a Changing Workplace
summary: SHRM President and CEO Johnny C. Taylor Jr. tells Bloomberg This Weekend how employers and workers can navigate open enrollment, AI-driven job disruption and growing generational divides in the workplace. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Taylor says companies need to communicate more clearly about benefits, help employees understand how AI can complement human intelligence and teach workers how to disagree constructively. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Persistent Oil Prices Threaten Inflation Outlook
summary: Seaport Research Partners Chief Equity Strategist Jonathan Golub tells Bloomberg This Weekend that stocks are not in an AI bubble, arguing that strong earnings and lower valuations show investors remain skeptical even as AI drives much of the market. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Golub says a prolonged Middle East conflict could keep oil and inflation elevated, eventually forcing the Federal Reserve to respond as strains emerge in credit markets. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Russian Diesel Deal Confronts Legal Uncertainty
summary: Oliver Wyman Geostrategy Practice Leader Daniel Tannebaum tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the first Russian diesel shipment under President Donald Trump’s deal with Vladimir Putin raises legal and compliance questions while offering limited relief for US fuel prices. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Tannebaum says private companies remain wary of doing business with Russia and warns that uncertainty over US sanctions and technology policy could push foreign governments and businesses toward alternatives to American suppliers. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: France Faces New Protests After Week of Violence
summary: Bloomberg News Paris Deputy Bureau Chief James Regan tells Bloomberg This Weekend that France is deploying tens of thousands of police and shifting protest routes as authorities try to prevent a repeat of last weekend’s violence and looting. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Regan says unrest that began with student demands has broadened into anger over the cost of living, threatening retailers and tourism as France also contends with fiscal and political strains. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Gershkovich Says Putin Seeks His Terms, Not a Deal
summary: Wall Street Journal foreign correspondent Evan Gershkovich tells Bloomberg This Weekend that he questions whether the Trump administration fully understands Vladimir Putin’s negotiating tactics after US envoy Steve Witkoff praised the Russian president as a “humanitarian” following Stephen Hubbard’s release. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Gershkovich draws on years covering Putin and his own 16 months in Russian custody to argue that the Russian leader remains focused on securing his demands for Ukraine rather than compromising in negotiations. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Oil Markets Brace for Renewed Iran Fighting
summary: Bloomberg Economics Chief Emerging Markets Economist Ziad Daoud tells Bloomberg This Weekend that the risk of renewed fighting between the US, Israel and Iran is rising, helping keep oil prices elevated even as energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz recover. Speaking with hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini, Daoud says the conflict could remain a long-term stalemate, with heightened shipping costs, depleted stockpiles and escalating regional tensions continuing to threaten global energy supplies. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Kenya Records Second Ebola Death as Uganda Restricts Transit
summary: Kenya has reported a second death from Ebola, a 65-year-old woman who was a close family member of the index case, while Uganda said it’s restricting transit for anyone with a history of travel to Democratic Republic of the Congo in an effort to halt the disease spreading.

summary: The house built by fixed income is facing an overhaul. Barclays Plc is showing it can do more for clients than trade bonds and arrange debt deals.

title: Indonesia Begins Trimming Pipeline Gas Exports to Singapore
summary: Indonesia is reducing natural gas exports to neighboring Singapore as President Prabowo Subianto seeks to shore up domestic supply and strengthen energy security for Southeast Asia’s largest economy.

title: Mauritius Carrier Looks at Narrow-Body Jets in Fleet Overhaul
summary: Mauritius’ state-owned carrier is planning to add single-aisle aircraft and review the planned acquisition of wide-body planes as part of a long-term strategy review.

title: India Regulator Orders Options Trainer Avadhut Sathe to Refund INR 5.46B
summary: India’s market regulator has ordered options trader Avadhut Sathe and his trading academy to refund 5.46 billion rupees ($57.5 million) to course participants after finding they provided unregistered investment advice and research services under the guise of stock market education.

title: Singapore Expands Haze Investigation to 10 Locally Based Firms
summary: Singapore expanded its investigation into haze-creating fires in Indonesia that have blanketed the city-state in smog, requesting information from 10 locally registered companies.

title: Iran Plots, Houthi Attacks Spur US Departure Orders in Mideast
summary: The US has ordered the departure of diplomatic personnel and adjusted staffing at embassies across the Middle East as a result of Iranian efforts to target Americans, as well as threats from Houthi militants in Yemen, according to an American official.

title: Growth, Value Stocks Set for Reshuffle as S&P Adopts New Rules

title: Wealth Tax Debate, Midterm Investing, AI Anxiety
summary: Bloomberg Money takes the pulse of your financial life, powered by the reporting of our global newsroom. Today's guests: Whitney Tilson, Stansberry Research Editor, and Stephanie Guild, Robinhood CIO. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Andrew Brandt on MLB Salary Cap Fight as World Series Begins
summary: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. He calls the matchup evidence for the players’ union that success is possible without a salary cap, while cautioning that owners may dismiss it as an unsustainable exception: smaller-market teams have little margin for error and can lose players to wealthier clubs in free agency. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

title: How Valterra's Forging the Future of Platinum | Chief Financial Officer
summary: Chief Financial Officers now play a critical role in shaping corporate strategy and positioning organizations to meet future challenges. This episode profiles Valterra Platinum CFO Sayurie Naidoo, who leads the world's largest company producing platinum group metals. One year after its demerger from Anglo American, the South African firm is looking ahead to develop new markets for PGMs as the adoption of battery electric vehicles threatens their primary area of demand. (Source: Bloomberg)
